notable_features.text: Romanian is the only member of the Eastern Romance sub-branch to survive as a major national language, having evolved from Vulgar Latin dialects that split from Western Romance between the 5th and 8th centuries, giving it a distinctively isolated position among Romance languages. It follows a basic subject-verb-object word order and has a relatively large phoneme inventory of 51 sounds. Its verb system marks five distinct tense/aspect categories, reflecting a rich grammatical marking of time and aspect inherited and elaborated from its Latin roots.
